acceptance.criterion_verbatim: The unlabelled bucket is handled deliberately. `sub_asset_class: None` is 1 row -- `2602335D` / TPG Inc, the known four-symptom row. It must not silently take a ramp colour that implies a sector.
acceptance.invocation: focused fixture carrying one row per sector plus the unmapped row, rendered on port 5199 and READ
acceptance.output_evidence: PASS, BUT ONLY AFTER ANDREW CAUGHT MY FIRST IMPLEMENTATION -- recorded because the first version passed the criterion's letter. I implemented it as 'unmapped returns null from sectorRampColor and keeps its existing colour', which satisfied the stated prohibition exactly: no ramp step, no implied position. IT WAS STILL WRONG. The existing colour WAS ASSET_CLASS_COLORS['Equity'], so an UNCLASSIFIED row rendered in the exact tone of a CLASSIFIED equity one -- the bucket was invisible AS unlabelled. His word: "'Other' should be much darker, should not just be same color as 'Equity'". Now SECTOR_UNMAPPED_COLOR = PALETTE.gray900 #111827, 5.2x darker than equity blue by relative luminance, and a NEUTRAL rather than a darker blue so it sits off the ramp and cannot read as 'the last sector'. Cash is NOT routed here and keeps its own amber asset-class colour. Verified by render: the TPG row shows near-black, plainly distinct from every equity row above it.
acceptance.denominator: 1 unmapped row of 114 (2602335D / TPG Inc); 1 cash category deliberately not routed to the unmapped colour.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a sector with ZERO rows. `Real Estate` is in both lists and absent from today's data. Show the ramp does not shift or mis-colour when a member of the ordered axis has no rows -- a ramp computed over PRESENT values instead of the DECLARED axis changes every colour whenever a sector empties.
acceptance.invocation: built a fixture with ALL 19 Financials rows deleted, re-rendered on port 5199, and compared every surviving sector's shade against the pre-drop render
acceptance.output_evidence: EXERCISED AND PASSED. Dropped all 19 Financials rows so that sector had ZERO, re-rendered, and EVERY SURVIVING SECTOR KEPT ITS EXACT SHADE -- Information Technology, Consumer Discretionary, Communication Services, Health Care, Industrials, Energy and Consumer Staples all unchanged; Financials simply absent. The ramp did not shift. STRUCTURAL REASON: the index is a pure function of position within DECLARED_SECTOR_AXIS over its FIXED length of 11, and that axis is Object.keys of a declared constant -- data cannot influence it. Real Estate is declared, has ZERO rows today, and holds its step (index 8) regardless. This is the criterion the issuer called load-bearing and they were right: a ramp built from present values looks perfect today and re-colours the whole column the first day a sector empties, which nobody would attribute to the ramp.
acceptance.denominator: 19 Financials rows removed; 11 declared axis members; 7 surviving sectors compared, 0 shifted.
